papers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
papers.problem: Computer agents cost too much when a top model runs every step, and small models alone often fail.
papers.fix: LEASH hands control to the strong model only when the small model looks unsure, and scores 73.66% task success.
papers.practicalUseCase: That matches the always-strong setup at 72.90% and cuts cost 19.2%, so send only hard steps to big models.
papers.limitation: It was tested on one benchmark, OSWorld, with four model families.

papers.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
papers.problem: Cheating agents can trick the code that grades them into giving full credit without doing the task.
papers.fix: A loop where one agent hacks and another repairs the grader sharply cuts attack success on three benchmarks.
papers.practicalUseCase: If your agent tests can be gamed, scores lie, so run a hack-and-fix loop before trusting results.
papers.limitation: The paper gives no single number here, and it covers only three agent benchmarks.

papers.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
papers.problem: Teams train sparse autoencoders on billions of tokens without knowing whether that much data is needed.
papers.fix: Less data nearly matches full quality, but matched features only rise from 2% at 5M tokens to 29% at 50M.
papers.practicalUseCase: Pick the data budget by your goal, and check that features repeat before you trust claims about them.
papers.limitation: The strongest number comes from one model setup, Gemma-2-2B with BatchTopK.

papers.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
papers.problem: Nobody knew whether the effects of sparse autoencoder features simply add up when combined.
papers.fix: Features mostly add up, and adding pair terms lifts rank fidelity from 0.5874 to 0.7790.
papers.practicalUseCase: Single-feature explanations miss interaction effects, so test feature pairs before you steer a model.
papers.limitation: Results cover 18 model and behavior settings, so other settings may differ.

papers.title: Sharīʿah Compliance in Malaysia’s Digital Payment Systems: Evidence from Expert Interviews
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.leadAuthor: Wan Anis Wan Mohd Assrudin et al.
papers.problem: Malaysia has rules for digital payments, yet experts still doubt that payment firms follow Sharia in practice.
papers.fix: Ten Sharia experts said non-bank payment providers have weaker governance, and flagged data risks and low consumer awareness.
papers.practicalUseCase: Check a payment app's Sharia governance yourself before you trust the label.
papers.limitation: It covers only Malaysia and ten expert interviews, so it shows views, not measured compliance.

papers.title: Interest Prohibitions and Contract Design in Medieval Christianity and Islam
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: People assume interest bans work the same everywhere, but medieval Europe and Islamic lands handled credit differently.
papers.fix: European lenders hid returns inside exchange or compensation, while Islamic contracts used trade, partnership, and clear risk sharing.
papers.practicalUseCase: Form can hide substance, so read the contract structure and who carries the risk, not the label.
papers.limitation: It rests on secondary sources and offers no new archive data.

papers.title: Financial Depth and Stability in Dual Banking Systems
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: It was unclear whether mixing Islamic and conventional banking helps the wider economy grow.
papers.fix: In 27 countries over 2010 to 2024, more Islamic finance raised private credit (beta 0.3725) and real output (beta 0.0842).
papers.practicalUseCase: Dual banking looks good for growth and small business credit, so policymakers can support it.
papers.limitation: It compares only dual-banking countries, not countries with a single banking system.

papers.title: Financing Government Issuances via Service Ownership Ṣukūk
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: Gulf governments face budget deficits and unemployment, and sukuk usually need physical assets behind them.
papers.fix: Sukuk backed by future public jobs cut the deficit 1.5 points of GDP and debt 4.3 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: If it holds up, governments could fund jobs with Sharia-compliant debt that costs 62 basis points less.
papers.limitation: It uses a model of six Gulf economies, so poorer Muslim-majority states need more study.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students may innovate less in the AI era, and standard motivation theories did not explain why.
papers.fix: Inner drive and outside rewards both boost research innovation, and good resources and confidence help most when motivation is low.
papers.practicalUseCase: Protect your own motivation first, then add support and resources to keep ideas moving.
papers.limitation: It uses one self-report survey at one time, so it cannot prove cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical training piles on tests and peer comparison, which may leave students feeling like frauds.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students worldwide, though results varied a lot by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud under pressure, you are far from alone, so talk about it early.
papers.limitation: Results varied widely between studies, so the pooled rate is only a rough guide.
